title: The almshouse of the Holy Spirit
chapter: II. The almshouse of the Holy Spirit

approval.notes: R-1318. Replaces the text title card in scripts/prologue/almshouse_opening.gd. Hands over to the observed spirit duel dialogue.prologue.almshouse_quarrel.

shots.caption: The almshouse of the Holy Spirit. Before first light.

lines.text: Fifteen winters old. No name worth writing in the parish book, no family to come for him.
lines.delivery: Same narrator as chapter I, closer and softer now. She is in the room.

lines.text: He wakes before the bell. He always wakes before the bell.
lines.delivery: The repetition is the point. Second half quieter.

authoring.direction: Introduce the hero by what nobody notices about him: he is the only one awake. Keep him small in the frame and off-centre. The room has to feel like charity, not cruelty - the Holy Spirit almshouse is a kindness that is also a dead end.
authoring.image_prompt: Cinematic film still, 40mm lens, asymmetrical off-centre composition, low eye-level wide interior of a long medieval almshouse hall before dawn. Two uneven rows of straw pallets on a beaten earth floor under a low smoke-stained timber ceiling, sleeping figures under coarse grey wool blankets, a wooden crutch leaning on a whitewashed limestone wall, a wooden bowl on the floor, a closed wooden shutter seeping thin blue pre-dawn light. A low tallow candle and the red embers of a small open hearth at the far right end provide the only warm light. Seated on his pallet well to the LEFT of frame, not centred, a thin fifteen-year-old boy with shoulder-length dark brown hair and a narrow pale Baltic face, wearing a loose coarse undyed linen tunic with no collar, no buttons and no pockets, laced at the throat, sits upright with the blanket across his lap, hands still, gazing sideways into the empty middle of the room, not at the camera. He is the only person awake. Cool filmic grade, amber ember accents against blue window light, heavy 35mm film grain, dust motes, damp cracked plaster, photographic realism.
authoring.video_prompt: 9 seconds. Camera: slow lateral pan right along the row of pallets at seated height, 40mm, ending with the boy entering frame right and settling slightly off-centre. Subject motion: sleepers breathing, one turning over; the candle flame leaning in a draught; embers pulsing; the boy completely still except for a single slow blink as the pan stops on him. No other movement. Audio: breathing, a chest cough from somewhere, wind in the shutter, no music until the pan reaches the boy, then one sustained high string. Voice-over only, no lip-sync. Narrator lines l1-l2; l2 landing exactly as the boy enters frame.
authoring.negative_prompt: text, watermark, modern hospital beds, metal bedframes, glass windows, bright lighting, clean linens, Victorian orphanage, nuns in modern habits, children's toys

lines.text: This is what he sees. Not instead of the room. On top of it.
lines.delivery: Careful and exact. This is the rule of the game being stated once.

lines.text: Shapes leaning over the sleeping. What they are afraid of, standing up out of them and breathing.
lines.delivery: Describing, not frightening. The horror is that it is ordinary to him.

lines.text: He learned early not to say so.
lines.delivery: Flat. The whole social cost of the gift in six words.

authoring.direction: The one supernatural frame in the prologue, and it must read as perception rather than as a monster scene. Same camera position as s01_hall so the audience understands it is the same room. Phantoms are cold cyan (ART_BIBLE moon cyan #58C7E8), translucent, bent over the sleepers with something like tenderness. Nothing attacks. The boy is looking straight at one.
authoring.image_prompt: Cinematic film still, 40mm lens, low eye-level interior of a long medieval almshouse hall before dawn: rows of straw pallets, sleeping figures under coarse grey wool blankets, whitewashed limestone wall, low timber ceiling, dim red embers at the far end. Faintly overlaid on the real room, barely there: three tall thin almost-transparent pale cyan apparitions bowed low over individual sleepers, long-limbed and faceless with suggestions of antlers and long fingers, smoke-like dissolving edges, very low opacity, desaturated ghostly blue-grey rather than bright, casting no shadow, laying only the faintest cold rim light on the blankets. Seated off-centre on his pallet, a thin fifteen-year-old boy with shoulder-length dark brown hair and a narrow pale Baltic face, in a loose coarse undyed linen tunic with no collar or buttons, looks calmly in profile at the nearest apparition. Dim two-colour light design, faint cold blue against low warm amber, very dark deep desaturated mid-tones, heavy 35mm film grain, volumetric smoke haze, photographic realism, subtle and restrained.
authoring.video_prompt: 10 seconds. Camera: slow push-in from the same position as the previous shot toward the boy, 40mm, settling on a loose medium of his face and the nearest apparition sharing frame. Subject motion: the apparitions breathing and swaying out of phase with the sleepers, one slowly turning its head toward the boy as the push-in arrives; smoke-like edges drifting; cyan rim light on a blanket pulsing with a sleeper's breath; the boy's eyes tracking the turning head, no other reaction. Audio: the room sound drops away almost completely, replaced by a low sub-bass pulse and a thin high metallic ring; one sleeper's breathing stays audible and in sync with the nearest apparition. Voice-over only, no lip-sync. Narrator lines l1-l3; l3 over a two-second held frame where the apparition and the boy simply look at each other.
authoring.negative_prompt: text, watermark, jump scare, screaming faces, blood, zombie, skull faces, Hollywood demon, saturated green or purple ghost light, lens flare, modern VFX glow

shots.caption: The matron and the porter, over bread.

lines.text: By the door the matron and the porter are arguing. It sounds like bread. It is not about bread.
lines.delivery: A faint smile in the voice. This is the lesson.

lines.text: Watch them, boy. Watch what they are really swinging at each other.
lines.delivery: Direct address to the hero and to the player at the same time. This is the tutorial prompt.

authoring.direction: Hand off into the observed spirit duel. The quarrel must be physically mundane and emotionally violent: no blows, two adults in a doorway, hands and jaw doing the work. The boy is foreground, out of focus, in the audience's seat - the same seat the player is about to take.
authoring.image_prompt: Cinematic film still, 85mm lens, very shallow depth of field, over-the-shoulder framing: extreme foreground lower left is the dark blurred out-of-focus head and shoulder of a seated fifteen-year-old boy with shoulder-length dark brown hair. Sharp in the middle distance, in a low rough timber doorway of a 14th-century almshouse with plank walls and iron strap hinges: a middle-aged matron in a dark brown wool kirtle, white linen head wrap and an iron ring of keys hanging at her belt, leaning in mid-shout, mouth open, one hand flat and cutting the air; facing her at close range a heavy-shouldered porter in a patched russet wool tunic and leather apron, shouting back, chin down, neck corded, holding a wicker bread basket low and turned away from her. Both furious, in profile, neither looking at the camera. The only lights are a small clay oil lamp with an open flame on a wooden wall bracket and cold dawn leaking through a closed plank shutter. Warm filmic grade, amber flame key light, cold blue fill, deep soft shadow, heavy 35mm film grain, photographic realism. Historically accurate Reval 1343.
authoring.video_prompt: 8 seconds. Camera: slow push-in past the boy's shoulder toward the doorway, 85mm, the foreground head sliding out of frame left as the move completes so the audience is pulled from his seat into the argument. Subject motion: the matron's cutting hand repeating twice, faster the second time; the porter's basket turning further away from her; both talking over each other, lips moving, speech deliberately inaudible under the voice-over; the key ring swinging; one listener on a pallet behind them rolling over to face the wall. Audio: hissed overlapping Low German and Estonian kept just below intelligibility, the key ring, a wicker creak; the string note from the previous shot cuts off hard on the word 'bread'. LIP-SYNC REQUIRED LATER for the matron and porter when their duel lines are voiced; for the still and first video tier their speech stays unintelligible and no sync is needed. Narrator lines l1-l2; l2 is the last thing heard before the sequence ends and the spirit duel opens.
authoring.negative_prompt: text, watermark, physical fight, slapping, weapons, blood, comic expressions, modern clothing, aprons with printed logos, clean white linen

source_notes.summary: A Holy Spirit priest is recorded in Reval in 1316; the Holy Spirit parish and its charitable hospital are the anchor for the prologue location.
A house for orphans and the destitute attached to the Holy Spirit parish is a composite of ordinary Hanseatic almshouse practice, not a specific 1343 attestation (ADR 0033 §7).

The protagonist, the matron, the porter, the apparitions over the sleepers and all narration are authored for ADR 0033 and R-1318. The spirit layer is presented as the hero's perception and is never confirmed as a diagnosis.
